title: Extension along an isomorphism is restriction along the inverse
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence], there is a natural
isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}
$$
of functors $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$.

proof.text: Put $R=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ and $I=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence], $R:\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ is an equivalence with quasi-inverse $I$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint] with $F=R$ and $G=I$: its left-adjoint clause supplies an adjunction $b:I\dashv R$. This uses the equivalence isomorphisms, rather than assuming arbitrary chosen quasi-inverse isomorphisms already satisfy the triangle identities.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: the inverse restriction is a quasi-inverse and hence a left adjoint; categorical fact as in Stacks Tags 001J and 0037, realized by the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: The hypotheses inherited from [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence] include all those of extension of scalars: $\mathcal C$ is braided, has coequalizers, both tensor functors preserve colimits, and $\mathcal R$ is commutative. Thus [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] applies to the same morphism $\varphi$ and supplies the adjunction $a:\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\dashv R$. Its statement identifies the left adjoint with the tensor-coequalizer extension functor used in the conclusion.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: extension of scalars is left adjoint to restriction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to the adjunctions $a$ and $b$ from steps 2 and 1, with $L_1=\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$, $L_2=I$, $R_1=R_2=R$ and $\delta=\mathrm{id}_R$. It gives a natural isomorphism $c:\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\xrightarrow{\sim}I$, characterized by $R(c_M)\circ\eta_{a,M}=\eta_{b,M}$. In particular, substituting the definition of $I$ gives the required natural isomorphism of functors $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: uniqueness of left adjoints compatible with their adjunctions; Stacks Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, via the cited Mathlib leaf
